rationale: The plan correctly diagnoses the fatal absence of replication, refuses default DESeq2/edgeR dispersion estimation, and makes log2 fold change on normalized counts the primary deliverable, which is the right instinct. However it then reintroduces a p-value/FDR column via an assumed fixed dispersion (0.1-0.4) or Poisson test; no matter how heavily caveated, this manufactures inferential output the design cannot support and invites exactly the misreading the caveats warn against, and the plan never names the replication level (>=3 per group) that would restore inference. QC is appropriate for n=2 (library sizes, detection rate, normalization factors) but there is no sample-distance or outlier policy, and the filter (CPM>1 in at least one sample) and TMM/size-factor normalization inside the workflow are explicit and reasonable. There is no design formula or stated reference level beyond the treated-vs-control direction, no shrinkage, and thresholds are applied post hoc to a fold-change ranking; enrichment names a versioned human WikiPathways GMT and the log2FC ranking metric but omits an ORA universe and gene-set size window.
